scope: Replace runtime SQLite memory with device-owned daily conversation files and sourced person profiles

runtime.database: isolated temporary SQLite for accounts and legacy migration only

implemented: Final user and assistant transcripts, operation outcomes and playback receipts recorded independently of lossy admin subscriptions
Original turn and item IDs retained for delayed transcripts, date partitioned by event time in Asia/Shanghai
Unknown speakers stay unattributed; explicit self-introductions and registered voice/face identities use stable person IDs
Versioned person sections with user sources, observed time, superseded history, expiry and complete management pagination
Conservative incremental first-person extraction with restart checkpoints; complex interpretation uses sourced Agent tools
Repeated facts merge source references, transient states renew only from newer evidence, delayed old evidence cannot replace newer corrections
Flecket per-response and tool-continuation profile loading; visible non-speakers expose basic information only
MOSS session background updates through its existing session.update protocol
Bounded and continuable Agent search, person listing and long-record reading
Linked forgetting removes sources, same-turn records and derived revisions; old memory epochs invalidate delayed writers and old playback/context
Device locks, atomic replacement, durable recovery journal, interrupted append recovery and idempotent writes
One-way resumable legacy SQLite/JSON export into unattributed file profiles; old sources removed only after file commits
Memory management page supports people, sections, source inspection, dates, search, pagination, correction and forgetting

limits: Automatic extraction is conservative rule-based processing plus normal Agent tool use; no additional local inference pipeline was introduced
MOSS update timing relative to an already-generating response requires upstream integration verification
Client reconnect does not independently prove erasure of upstream-provider logs, backups or provider-managed persistent history
Whole-device erase coordination follows the project's single-process runtime binding
